title: ChatGPT Review Package — Input
description: The bounded package a human exports to ChatGPT. No AI API is called by this repository; the package is generated, handed to a human, and the returned assessment is imported and validated separately. The package must never contain secrets, private company information, unbounded article text, or raw licensed content that cannot be shared.

evidence_records.description: Bounded evidence items. Each carries an evidence_id the returned assessment must reference; an assessment referencing an unknown evidence_id is rejected on import.

required_output_binding_instructions.description: WO-010-R3 §1: tells whoever pastes this package which five fields the returned output must echo verbatim (see required_output_binding below), and that produced_at is not one of them.

exclusions_applied.description: What was deliberately withheld from the package (secrets, private company information, unbounded article text, restricted raw content). Recorded so a reviewer can see the boundary was applied.

required_output_binding.description: WO-010-R3 §1: the same five values as literals, restated here (not only as instructions) so a script diffing an output against its package has one well-known location to read, and a human pasting the package can copy them directly.

dataset.description: Which publication surface this package was built from. Only a current_publication package may be approved into the current AI Outlook.

package_purpose.description: What the package is for. Must agree with the dataset: a technical_demo package is an engine demonstration however it is labelled.

source_cutoff.description: The instant the underlying source records were selected against. Recorded separately from data_cutoff_at so an approval can detect an assessment produced against a different vintage of the same package. WO-010-R6 §6: null when the package includes zero acquisition-bound evidence -- never silently replaced with as_of_time/data_cutoff_at.

provenance_summary.description: Where the package's contents came from, and how many records the qualification filter excluded. Lets a reviewer and the approval gate see the provenance mix without re-deriving it.

acquisition_summary.description: WO-010-R5 §9. What actually stands behind this package's current evidence: which collection runs and manual-review events it drew on, how many otherwise-qualified records were excluded for having no acquisition binding, and the latest source cutoff those bindings support. Present on every package (technical_demo packages report empty/zero values honestly rather than omitting the section) so a reviewer or the approval gate can independently confirm the package's evidence is not merely labelled live/reviewed but is actually traceable to a persisted acquisition event.

excluded_unbound_record_count.description: How many otherwise-qualified live_retrieved/human_reviewed_manual records were excluded from this package specifically because they carried no matching, valid acquisition binding.

latest_source_cutoff.description: The latest timestamp among this package's own qualifying acquisition bindings. Null when the package includes no acquisition-bound evidence.

collection_run_manifest_hashes.description: WO-010-R6 §4. output_manifest_sha256 of each qualifying collection run, keyed by run_id.

manual_review_record_set_hashes.description: WO-010-R6 §4. reviewed_record_set_sha256 of each qualifying manual review event, keyed by event_id.

included_current_record_ids.description: WO-010-R6 §4. record_id/evidence_id of every record this package's acquisition summary actually included.

live_record_bindings.description: WO-010-R7 §4. Per-record confirming/governing detail for every included live_retrieved record: which run was actually cited (confirming_run_id), which successful run's manifest actually backs it (governing_run_id), that run's own output_manifest_sha256 (never null), and the full supersedes_chain walked to resolve it. A not_modified binding is fully traceable here rather than collapsed into a single run-id-to-hash mapping that could otherwise show a null hash for the cited run while silently relying on another one.

acquisition_state_sha256.description: WO-010-R6 §4, made mandatory by WO-010-R7 §7. One hash covering every collection run and manual review event this build loaded -- not only the ones this package cites -- so approval-time revalidation can require an exact match against acquisition state read fresh from disk. Always a non-null SHA-256: a current package hashes its real acquisition state, and a technical-demo package uses the explicit canonical empty-state hash (collectors.collection_runs.EMPTY_ACQUISITION_STATE_SHA256) rather than null, so this field is never absent or ambiguous on any package.
